eyebrow: Keyword arguments -- calling a function by name
code:
def build_order_summary(order_id, customer_name, status="Shipped"):
    return f"Order {order_id} ({customer_name}) — {status}"

# positional -- relies on order
print(build_order_summary(1001, "Dana Whitfield"))

# keyword -- explicit, and order no longer matters
print(build_order_summary(customer_name="Marcus Ibeh", order_id=1002, status="Cancelled"))
caption: status="Cancelled" documents what that value means in a way a bare string in the third position never could.
Inside the function, line_totals is a regular tuple -- loop over it, sum it, or index into it like any other tuple.
extra_fields is a regular dict -- this exact pattern is how pd.DataFrame() and many library constructors are built.
